core_obligations: Show that the second, third and fourth formulations are equivalent, using that a weak ideal of definition lies in the Jacobson radical and that faithful flatness of a flat map can be tested modulo such an ideal (proof lines 4504-4511).
Show that surjectivity of the morphism implies the third formulation: each quotient map is the base change of the morphism along a quotient of the target, hence surjective (proof lines 4511-4516).

Show the converse: a morphism from a quasi-compact scheme into the target factors through a quotient, so the base change of the morphism along that quotient is surjective because the corresponding quotient map is, whence the morphism is surjective (proof lines 4516-4524).
proof_roadmap: Equivalence of the ring-theoretic formulations (proof lines 4504-4511).
Surjectivity implies the quotient maps are faithfully flat (proof lines 4511-4516).
Converse by factorisation through a quotient (proof lines 4516-4524).
difficulty_reason: In the situation of the structure lemma for etale morphisms over a McQuillan space, the lemma asserts the equivalence of the surjectivity of the morphism, faithful flatness of the corresponding map of algebras, and faithful flatness of that map after passing to the quotient by any, or by some, weak ideal of definition (statement lines 4491-4502). The proof first shows that the last three formulations agree: a weak ideal of definition consists of topologically nilpotent elements, so it lies in the Jacobson radical, and for a flat map faithful flatness may be tested after quotienting by an ideal contained in the radical (proof lines 4504-4511). It then relates the first formulation to the third: surjectivity of the morphism implies that each of the morphisms between the spectra of the quotients, which is the base change of the morphism along a quotient of the target, is surjective, which is faithful flatness of the corresponding ring map (proof lines 4511-4516). Conversely, assuming the quotient maps are faithfully flat, a morphism from a quasi-compact scheme into the target factors through a quotient, and the base change of the morphism along that quotient is surjective, whence the morphism itself is surjective (proof lines 4516-4524). The claim is H2: the equivalence among the ring-theoretic formulations is a short transfer, and the geometric equivalence uses the factorisation of test morphisms through a quotient together with the stability of surjectivity under base change.
